\/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERoll no. 96\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003EHI ,\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is PRATHYUSHA MULUKALA ,A medical student from Telangana, India.I am here to share a few experiences that I have learnt from medicine clinical postings.There are case blogs done by me with the help of pgs from second year to until now that are mentioned in my blog,which are inspired by Dr. Rakesh biswas sir.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/prathyushamulukala666.blogspot.com\/?m=1\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECBBLE PAJR PARTICIPATORY LEARNING ACTION RESEARCH DISCLAIMER\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;NOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS\/HER GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThese blogs encouraged me to show a special interest in taking detailed history and clinical examination which I am not perfect at first . It helped me to take each and every minute detail of the patient and their history ,there actual problem from the start. A disease is slow process that it starts way before showing actual symptoms. When we take a detailed history with patient way of living and everything,it may lead to the actual diagnosis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI will start with my first experience,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhen I am in second year I have posted in medicine for the first time, I was so excited about the clinical postings to learn some new things.At first I went to OPD of medicine, then a patient came into the OPD with complaints of unable to walk properly and with tremors of hands since 1 year,when sir asked the patient to walk for some distance ,the patient walked with short steps and on examination there was rigidity over extremities and by the past history known that he already using levodopa and carbidopa medications.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd that was the first time I saw a clinical case and learned how to examine the patient, At that time I was known that by the gait of the patient we can diagnose some diseases .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt was the time that physiology classes learnt in first year turned into the actual clinical case with parkinsonism symptoms and signs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFrom that day I understood that we can learn lot from OPD .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDuring those days we have known how to do a pleural tap from pgs ,they have explained us while doing the procedure.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd bone marrow aspiration procedure also\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EObserved.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd I have done ascitic tap in second year under guidance of pgs ,that was the first procedure I have done in my undergraduation .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EExamining the patient was the most favourite part of mine which I have learnt in medicine postings and it is very important part in diagnosing a case.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhen I entered into internship first of all I don't what to do but I looked forward to learn more from the medicine clinical postings.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFirst I did ICU duties -where I have learnt about the ventilator cases,about intubation,how to intubate a patient.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd mainly GCS of the patient and higher mental function, extubation criteria.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMost of the cases what I have observed is that the ventilator cases are more\u0026nbsp; prone to ventilator associated pneumonia infections which has to be taken into consideration.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHow to take an ABG sample and interpretation of ABG.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd management of diabetic ketoacidosis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EVitals play most important role for a patient,where we can manage by seeing vitals for example a patient Blood pressure is dropping immediate action is needed so that patient doesn't go into shock\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd how to read ECG\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENext I have done done nephrology duties - where I have learnt how to keep central line and about hemodialysis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd about chronic kidney disease and management.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Esome of the points I have learnt in clinical postings from\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/prathyushamulukala666.blogspot.com\/2022\/06\/a-55-yr-old-female-with-fever-neck.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*The above case is a meningitis case , from this case I have learnt\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECNS EXAMINATION:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Higher mental functions\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*GCS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEye response\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- opens spontaneously -4\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- To commands -3\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-To pain-3\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026nbsp; No response\u0026nbsp; -1\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EVerbal\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-oriented well to time ,person,place-5\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-confused state-4\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-inappropriate words -3\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-incomprehensible sounds-2\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-no response-1\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMotor response\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-obeys commands-6\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-moves to localised pain-5\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-flex to withdraw from pain-4\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-abnormal flexion-3\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-abnormal extension -2\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-no response-1\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* How to do Cranial nerve examination\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Meningeal signs examination\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- neck stiffness\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- brudzinki sign\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- kernigs sign\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Sensory examination\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Motor examination\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- power ,bulk , movements of the muscle\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Reflexes examination\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Difference between rigidity and spasticity\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd learnt about upper motor neuron lesions and lower motor neuron lesions .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Cerebellar examination - gait ,rombergs sign.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Learnt How to make a Fever chart\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* About lumbar puncture and how to do analysis of CSF report and interpretation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/prathyushamulukala666.blogspot.com\/2023\/02\/60-year-old-male-with-pain-abdomen.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFrom the above case; learning points are-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis a case of 60 yr old male complaining with abdominal pain in umbilical region ,left upper quadrant region which relieves on bending forward.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPain relieves on bending forward is a classical symptom of acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn examination the patient doesn't have grey Turner's sign or Cullen sign.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGrey Turner's sign - discoloration of flanks\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECullen sign - discoloration over periumbilical region.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAbdominal examination - i learnt how to examine for abdominal distension(ascitic fluid ) by following tests;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EShifting dullness,puddle sign,fluid thrill\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELab investigation interpretation in pancreatitis and ultrasound findings - peri pancreatic edema and bulky pancreas\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EManagement -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*At first nil by mouth for this patient - so I Put a ryles tube ,learnt how to insert ryles tube - I asked the patient to sit and flex the neck and ryles tube with lignocaine under aseptic conditions I inserted the tube through nose and asked the patient to swallow while inserting, and checked for correct position of the tube i;e in the stomach by\u0026nbsp; pushing the air through the tube ,on auscultation we can hear the sound,this says tube is in correct place.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFor some cases like pancreatitis and other psychosocial cases ...methods of diversion from alcohol intake, depression from financial status and other situations... the way of counseling the patient is quite encouraging.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/prathyushamulukala666.blogspot.com\/2023\/03\/35-yo-male-with-complaints-of-vomitings.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is a case of 35 y\/o male with complaints of vomitings ,6-7 episodes in a day.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe is known diabetic.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo other complaints are present.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI learnt how to manage a case of diabetic ketosis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is a case where metabolic disturbance is absent,there is no acidosis or alkalosis in this patient. RTA WITH INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E26th March 2023\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr. M. Prathyusha ( Intern )\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERoll no : 96\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECASE :\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E25 YEAR OLD MALE PATIENT BROUGHT TO CASUALTY WITH H\/O FALL FROM BIKE UNDER ALCOHOL INFLUENCE AT 9:30 PM NEAR HALIYA,NALGONDA ON 20\/03\/23.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAND THEN TAKEN TO HOSPITAL FOR FURTHER MANAGEMENT.PATIENT IS INVESTIGATED AND DIAGNOSED TO HAVE RTA , TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY,WITH INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE WITH FRONTAL BONE FRACTURE WITH ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA AND RIGHT FRONTAL LACERATION SOFT TISSUE REPAIR WITH DEBRIDEMENT WAS DONE ON 20\/3\/23.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPATIENT WAS INTUBATED ON 20\/3\/23 I\/V\/O POOR GCS WITH FIO2: 100% MODE: VC WITH ANTIEPILEPTIC MEDICATIONS.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPATIENT IS SEDATED AND PARALYSED\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHR: 101\/MIN\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBP: 130\/80 MMHG\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECVS: S1S2+\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ER\/S: BAE+, B\/L CREPTS +\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPUPILS: SLUGGISH RTL, ASYMMETRICAL SPO2: 98% WITH FIO2: 100%\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETEMP: Afebrile\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFOCAL SEIZURES+ (ON \u0026amp; OFF)\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMYOCLONIC JERKS (ON \u0026amp; OFF)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMENTIONED COMPLAINTS, PATIENT IS EXAMINED AND ALL NECESSARY INVESTIGATIONS WERE DONE.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EON EXAMINATION: (20\/03\/2023) PATIENT IS NOT RESPONDING TO ORAL COMMANDS BUT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESPONTANEOUS MOVEMENTS ARE PRESENT\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2 D ECHO SHOWN NORMAL STUDY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGCS:\u0026nbsp;
